threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think 15 minutes to the Tube is a reasonable walk; locals know that's just a warm-up for the wait at the platform.
Caught the 345 last night, bus driver treated it like a go-kart race. Also, saw a guy serenading a sleeping passenger with a ukulele. Classic Brixton!

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I saw a toddler calmly feeding pigeons while a group of skaters smuggled in beers from the kiosk. That's Neukölln for you.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Friedrichshain can you find a bar in an old butcher shop that serves vegan currywurst alongside craft beer. It’s a wild blend of past and present.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s local when they instinctively duck under the BART tracks at Civic Center, avoiding the smoke and chaos like it’s just another Tuesday.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught the Muni stuck at Civic Center yesterday—dog on the tracks while a guy recited Shakespeare. Only in SF, right?

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists assume all the street performers are locals, but many come from outside just to capitalize on our numerous festivals.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by their bewilderment at how to find the 'actual' bus stops in Gràcia — they always stand near the wrong intersections.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think you can get through a Saturday without pondering which farmer's market has the best sourdough and hipster jam.
Last night on the 43, a bloke serenaded the entire bus with a ukulele. Even the grannies were nodding along. Only in Brockley.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When you hear a busker playing techno on the corner while a group of older folks dance in the middle of the street—it's quintessential Neukölln.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg will you find a kebab shop that opens at 3 AM just for the club crowd, serving both drunk revellers and the morning commuters.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can tell a local by how they know to avoid Dolores Park on sunny weekends—too many tech bros with their speaker setups.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught the bus yesterday with a guy practicing his stand-up act. Best part was the punchline about dodging Muni delays—got a round of applause!

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is all about the plaça, but it's the hidden bars on side streets where the real vibe is. That's where the locals unwind.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can always tell a newcomer by their hesitation at the metro turnstiles; only the locals know to push through without thinking.
